title: DecisionRecorded producer is 'all 19' but the event type and ledger have one owner
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 42 (A2 event catalogue 1/2) row 08; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events EV-08
description: Arch v5 lists all 19 services as producer of DecisionRecorded on the shared topic rwb.decision-record.v1, while the legacy owning module is the decision center and log. A single owner is needed for the event type, topic and ledger; the map records rwb-decision.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 08 producer 'all 19'; slide 20 'DecisionRecorded -> rwb.decision-record.v1 (ledger in rwb-decision)'; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-08 owning module Decision center and log.
proposed: Own the rwb.decision-record.v1 topic and the central ledger in rwb-decision (P7); every service publishes its own local decision record

title: TimerDue producer is a durable timer, not a rwb-case event
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 42 (A2 event catalogue 1/2) row 18; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events EV-18
description: Arch v5 retires TimerDue ('timer inside the workflow') and gives the producer as a durable timer; the legacy owning module is Case and workflow. The map records the Temporal workflow kit (PLT) as owner and keeps TimerBreached with rwb-case.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 42 row 18 producer 'durable timer', consumer '-', state retired; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-18 owning module Case and workflow.
proposed: Treat TimerDue as a durable timer in the workflow kit (PLT); no service publishes it

title: PartnerResultSubmitted direction and owner
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 43 (A3 event catalogue 2/2) row 21; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events EV-21
description: Arch v5 makes rwb-partner the producer of PartnerResultSubmitted; the legacy design marks it consumed from the partner portal. The partner portal is the external channel, so rwb-partner (S9) owns the event.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 row 21 producer rwb-partner, consumers rwb-litigation, rwb-asset and rwb-case; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-21 direction Consumed, owning module Partner portal.
proposed: Own PartnerResultSubmitted in rwb-partner (S9); the partner portal stays the external channel

title: AceDataReady direction and owner
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 43 (A3 event catalogue 2/2) row 26; Event and Messaging Design v4 Events EV-26
description: Arch v5 makes rwb-source-data the producer of AceDataReady from the ACE batch record; the legacy design marks it consumed from ACE ingestion. ACE ingestion stays outside the 19 services, so rwb-source-data (P1) owns the event.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 43 row 26 producer rwb-source-data; slide 15 OUT topic rwb.source-data.events.v1; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-26 direction Consumed, owning module ACE ingestion.

title: Timer check retired, but the decision log keeps Quartz and the TimerScheduler
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Decision Log v10; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) JOB-05; Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T2; ADR-011
description: Arch v5 retires JOB-05 (durable timers inside each workflow, owner all); Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T2 and ADR-011 keep Quartz and the TimerScheduler port for Epic 1 and Epic 2. Arch v5 wins, so no Temporal Schedule is recorded and the durable-timer kit is PLT.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-05 owner all, mechanism 'durable timers (retired)'; Decision Log v10 D-RCV-36 T2; ADR-011 (Quartz and Spring Batch keep every Epic 1 and Epic 2 job; JOB-05 runs behind the TimerScheduler port).
proposed: Retire JOB-05; durable timers in the workflow kit (PLT) replace the 5-minute check

title: WIN notices have two owners in the job map
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) JOB-10; slide 31 notes; slide 17
description: Arch v5 gives JOB-10 two owners, rwb-comms and rwb-integration. The map needs one owner: rwb-comms (P6) owns the notice and the 16:00 window; rwb-integration (P2) delivers the file as a step.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-10 owner 'rwb-comms + integration'; slide 31 notes 'rwb-comms with rwb-integration'; slide 17 P6 OUT 'Integration: deliverFile (WIN letters)'.
proposed: Own JOB-10 in rwb-comms (P6) with deliverFile in rwb-integration (P2)

title: Decision log copy: continuous Kafka ingest versus the nightly data-lake job
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) JOB-13; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs JOB-13; R-PREC DP-17
description: Arch v5 makes decision-log ingest continuous on Kafka in rwb-decision and removes the data lake (DP-17); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 still copies the log to the data lake nightly at 01:00. Arch v5 wins; no Temporal Schedule is recorded.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-13 owner rwb-decision, mechanism 'ingest is continuous (Kafka)'; R-PREC DP-17 removes the data lake and INT-19/INT-20; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-13 nightly 01:00 to the data lake.
proposed: Continuous DecisionRecorded ingest in rwb-decision (P7); no data-lake copy

title: Reporting extract: Airflow trigger versus the 01:30 Schedule and the data lake
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) JOB-15; slide 31 notes; slide 15; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs JOB-15
description: Arch v5 slide 44 (job map) makes JOB-15 an Airflow trigger with no data lake, while the slide 31 notes and slide 15 describe a 01:30 Temporal Schedule measures, and Batch and Scheduling Design v4 writes the extract to the data lake for Power BI. The catalogue wins; rwb-reporting (P9) owns the extract and runs the buildRegulatoryExtract activity.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-15 mechanism 'Airflow trigger (no data lake)'; slide 31 notes 'measures 01:30 (rwb-reporting, JOB-15)'; slide 15 'Schedule: measures 01:30'; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-15 data lake and Power BI.
proposed: Airflow-triggered buildRegulatoryExtract in rwb-reporting (P9); no data lake

title: Write-off scan: Temporal Schedule versus the ACE batch trigger and Quartz
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1; Recovery Workbench Batch and Scheduling Design v4
section: Arch v5 slide 44 (A4 job map) JOB-16; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 23; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 Jobs JOB-16
description: Arch v5 slide 44 and the Temporal design make JOB-16 a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff on the 3rd working day; Batch and Scheduling Design v4 starts it on the ACE batch-complete record and the T2 open point keeps Quartz. Arch v5 wins; S7 owns the Schedule.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 44 JOB-16 owner rwb-writeoff, mechanism Schedule; Temporal and Drools Design v1 slide 23 (JOB-16 is a Temporal Schedule in rwb-writeoff; phase 1 note T2 keeps Quartz); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-16 on the ACE batch-complete record.
proposed: Temporal Schedule write-off scan in rwb-writeoff (S7) on the 3rd working day
